title: Fixed Phrases with “and”
description: Learn fixed word pairs that make everyday English more natural.
objectives: Keep fixed phrases in their usual order

source.title: Advanced Grammar & Vocabulary — Express Publishing
source.note: Lesson explanations, examples and practice have been adapted for independent study from the supplied unit. Answers and explanations are editorial, not a publisher answer key.

lessons.title: Fixed order matters
lessons.body: Many expressions join words with and. Their meaning and order are conventional: learn the whole expression rather than translating one word at a time.
examples: safe and sound, not sound and safe
odds and ends, not ends and odds

lessons.title: Meaning may be figurative
lessons.body: The whole phrase may mean more than the individual words. By and large means generally; ins and outs means detailed information.
examples: By and large, the plan worked.
Explain the ins and outs of the system.

lessons.title: Fit the phrase into the sentence
lessons.body: Some phrases behave like adverbs, some like nouns and others like adjectives. Learn the surrounding grammar along with the pair.
examples: The car is her pride and joy.
It is part and parcel of the job.

lessons.title: Hyphens and fixed forms
lessons.body: Use hyphens when a compound acts as a single adjective before a noun where needed. The normal expression after a verb can look different.

lessons.title: Choose the right situation
lessons.body: Touch and go suggests uncertainty about an important outcome. Wear and tear is deterioration from normal use. These expressions are more specific than “uncertain” or “damage”.
examples: It was touch and go whether the rescue would succeed.
The chairs show ordinary wear and tear.

vocabulary.definition: Accept an unpleasant situation without complaining.
vocabulary.example: We had to grin and bear it.

vocabulary.definition: The details of a complicated situation.
vocabulary.example: She explained the ins and outs of the contract.
vocabulary.note: Usually the ins and outs of.

vocabulary.example: Do not make a song and dance about the delay.
vocabulary.note: Usually make a song and dance about.

vocabulary.example: A drawer held a few odds and ends.

vocabulary.definition: Finally and decisively, ending doubt or repetition.
vocabulary.example: Let us settle this once and for all.
He is your own flesh and blood.
That is an out-and-out lie.
Revision is part and parcel of learning.
I need some peace and quiet.
Her garden is her pride and joy.

vocabulary.definition: Very formal, conventional and easily shocked.
vocabulary.example: She was too prim and proper for the joke.
There was pushing and shoving at the entrance.

vocabulary.definition: Safe and unharmed after possible danger.
vocabulary.example: The missing hikers returned safe and sound.
vocabulary.note: Often after arrive, return or be found.

vocabulary.example: We left the kitchen spick and span.
vocabulary.note: US variant spic and span is also used.

vocabulary.definition: Uncertain, especially for a serious outcome.
vocabulary.example: It was touch and go for a while.
vocabulary.note: Often it was touch and go whether.

vocabulary.example: An up-and-coming musician played tonight.
Every friendship has its ups and downs.
The carpet shows some wear and tear.
We were well and truly lost.

vocabulary.definition: Honestly and according to the rules.
vocabulary.example: They won fair and square.

exerciseGroups.title: Vocabulary recall
exerciseGroups.instruction: Choose the word or phrase that matches the meaning.

questions.explanation: Donations came in dribs and drabs. Often after in.

questions.prompt: Very early, with a positive sense of readiness.
questions.explanation: We set off bright and early. Often with leave, start or get up.
By and large, the course was useful. Often introduces a general judgement.
Affordable flats are few and far between. Usually after be.

questions.prompt: Accept an unpleasant situation without complaining.
questions.explanation: We had to grin and bear it. Informal.

questions.prompt: The details of a complicated situation.
questions.explanation: She explained the ins and outs of the contract. Usually the ins and outs of.
Do not make a song and dance about the delay. Usually make a song and dance about.
A drawer held a few odds and ends. Plural noun phrase.

questions.prompt: Finally and decisively, ending doubt or repetition.
questions.explanation: Let us settle this once and for all. Not simply one time.
He is your own flesh and blood. Often own flesh and blood.
That is an out-and-out lie. Compound adjective; often negative.
Revision is part and parcel of learning. Usually part and parcel of.
I need some peace and quiet. Uncountable phrase.
Her garden is her pride and joy. Usually possessive + pride and joy.

questions.prompt: Very formal, conventional and easily shocked.
questions.explanation: She was too prim and proper for the joke. Describes a person or manner.
There was pushing and shoving at the entrance. Usually describes a crowd.

questions.prompt: Safe and unharmed after possible danger.
questions.explanation: The missing hikers returned safe and sound. Often after arrive, return or be found.
We left the kitchen spick and span. US variant spic and span is also used.

questions.prompt: Uncertain, especially for a serious outcome.
questions.explanation: It was touch and go for a while. Often it was touch and go whether.
An up-and-coming musician played tonight. Compound adjective.
Every friendship has its ups and downs. Plural noun phrase.
The carpet shows some wear and tear. Different from deliberate damage.
We were well and truly lost. Emphatic.

questions.prompt: Honestly and according to the rules.
questions.explanation: They won fair and square. Often with win or beat.
